title: SCOBY-D1 low-cost multifunctional skin research roadmap with closed evidence gates
scope: Non-weaponized materials-science roadmap for developing and comparing low-cost SCOBY-derived sheet materials and composites. The program focuses on material identity, mechanical behavior, moisture durability, adhesion, surface functionality, electromagnetic compatibility, thermal aging, manufacturability, cost and reproducibility. It does not establish or provide a recipe for ballistic armor, weapon protection, electronic-warfare systems, jamming, stealth, or operational drone countermeasures.
program_goal: Determine whether SCOBY-derived sheet materials can become a credible low-cost sustainable skin or shell material for benign enclosures, wearable prototypes, packaging, robotics housings, educational structures, interior panels, or other non-weaponized applications.

items: Predictions of specific shotgun or fragment resistance
Operational electronic-warfare attenuation targets tied to particular bands
Predicted drone-control disruption or countermeasure performance
Specific weapon-testing distances, loads, or pass/fail criteria
Claims that a particular nanofiller loading guarantees a given shielding level
Claims that a particular laminate will stop projectiles without validated standards testing
what_to_remove_from_prior_concept.reason: These claims over-specify performance before material identity, process control and independent characterization, and they shift the program toward weapon-protection and electronic-warfare optimization rather than a credible low-cost biomaterial research program.

TRACK_01_MATERIAL_IDENTITY.goal: Establish what the dried or modified SCOBY-derived material actually is before selecting applications.

TRACK_02_MECHANICAL_SKIN.goal: Build the cheapest useful SCOBY skin before adding expensive functional fillers.
candidate_architectures: cross-laminated two-layer skin with orthogonal orientation
SCOBY surface layer on a conventional benign substrate
tests: puncture resistance as a generic materials metric
peel or interlaminar adhesion where layered

TRACK_03_MOISTURE_AND_AGING.goal: Solve the biggest practical weakness of cellulose-based leather-like materials: water and environmental durability.
candidate_strategies: natural wax or lipid-compatible finishes where appropriate
tests: mold or biodegradation tendency under controlled non-pathogenic test conditions
TRACK_03_MOISTURE_AND_AGING.gate: No leather-like durability claim until wet-state retention and cyclic aging are measured against a conventional low-cost benchmark.

TRACK_04_SURFACE_AND_TOUCH.goal: Make the material commercially plausible as a skin rather than merely a laboratory film.
tests: odor or volatile release screening where relevant

TRACK_05_LOW_COST_COMPOSITES.goal: Find reinforcements that improve performance without making the material economically absurd or hard to process.
preferred_candidates: water-based benign polymer binders or coatings
TRACK_05_LOW_COST_COMPOSITES.selection_rule: Prefer abundant, low-cost, low-toxicity reinforcements before advanced nanomaterials.

TRACK_06_EM_COMPATIBILITY.goal: Study electromagnetic compatibility as a passive materials property without targeting electronic-warfare or operational disruption.
safe_scope: shielding of a benign enclosure against laboratory interference
reduction of accidental coupling into sensors or instrumentation
comparison of conductive versus non-conductive coatings
frequency-dependent transmission and reflection measurements in calibrated fixtures
measurements: reflection and transmission in a controlled laboratory fixture
TRACK_06_EM_COMPATIBILITY.claim_boundary: No operational jammer, drone-control, stealth, radar-evasion, or electronic-warfare performance claim is admitted.

TRACK_07_THERMAL_AND_FIRE_BEHAVIOR.goal: Establish whether practical enclosures made from SCOBY skin are thermally stable and safe enough for intended benign environments.
tests: limited-scale ignition or flammability screening under appropriate laboratory controls
smoke and odor characterization where relevant
TRACK_07_THERMAL_AND_FIRE_BEHAVIOR.gate: No consumer or enclosure-use claim until thermal and flammability behavior is characterized for the intended application.

TRACK_08_MANUFACTURABILITY.goal: Close the gap between a clever sample and a repeatable cheap material.

preprocessing_matrix.priority_rule: For first-generation cheap skin development, prioritize baseline, B, and C; A, D, and E remain secondary research branches because they introduce additional process and safety complexity.

GEN0.purpose: Establish baseline mechanical, moisture, surface and aging behavior.

GEN1.description: Tension-dried SCOBY skin with controlled thickness and no advanced filler
GEN1.purpose: Measure whether process control alone improves consistency and handling.

GEN2.description: Cross-laminated SCOBY skin with orientation rotation
GEN2.purpose: Test whether simple architecture improves tear resistance and dimensional stability.

GEN3.description: SCOBY plus inexpensive cellulose or textile-fiber reinforcement
GEN3.purpose: Increase toughness and reduce the need for expensive nanomaterials.

GEN4.description: GEN2 or GEN3 plus a benign water-resistant surface treatment
GEN4.purpose: Address the main practical weakness without changing the structural core.

GEN5.description: Laboratory conductive composite for electromagnetic-compatibility studies
GEN5.purpose: Determine whether a thin conductive skin can provide measurable passive shielding while preserving acceptable mechanical properties.

design_of_experiments.stage_1: Screen baseline, untensioned drying, tensioned drying, and one low-cost reinforcement family.
design_of_experiments.stage_2: Optimize the best two architectures for moisture durability and tear resistance.
design_of_experiments.stage_3: Add one surface treatment family and test aging.
design_of_experiments.stage_4: Only after mechanical and environmental gates pass, investigate passive EM compatibility properties.
design_of_experiments.replication: At least three independent specimen preparations per condition for exploratory screening; increase replication for final comparisons.
design_of_experiments.blocking: Randomize specimen order or block by SCOBY production batch to reduce batch effects.
design_of_experiments.blind_measurement: Where practical, characterize coded specimens without revealing formulation or expected ranking to the operator.

mechanical: commercial plant-based leather substitute where available
benchmark_matrix.comparison_rule: A SCOBY material should be judged against the cheapest plausible competing material for the same benign application, not against an idealized advanced material.

G0_IDENTITY.criterion: Material identity must be assigned provisionally from measured composition, morphology, density, moisture and mass balance while preserving alternatives.

G1_PROCESS_HISTORY.criterion: Every sample receives a complete preprocessing and drying history with batch, geometry, moisture, temperature, humidity, fixture and storage metadata.

G2_STRUCTURE.criterion: Morphology, thickness, density, porosity where relevant and surface chemistry are measured before function is claimed.

G3_MECHANICAL_FUNCTION.criterion: Strength, elongation, tear, puncture, wet retention and fatigue are tested against matched controls.

G4_ENVIRONMENTAL_DURABILITY.criterion: Wet-dry, humidity, UV and thermal aging are included before durability claims.

G5_EM_COMPATIBILITY.criterion: Passive laboratory EMC/shielding characterization only; no operational EW, jammer, stealth or control-disruption claims.

G6_MANUFACTURABILITY.criterion: Yield, cost per area, batch variation and process complexity must be quantified.

G7_APPLICATION.criterion: Only benign application classes with evidence-supported performance may be admitted after identity, structure, function, durability and reproducibility gates pass.

G8_CLAIM.criterion: Claims are limited to the strongest supported evidence and explicitly state uncertainty and benchmark context.

recommended_application_targets: wearable prototype covers where skin-contact safety is separately established
sensor housings and passive EMC enclosures where safety and EMC requirements are defined
acoustic or vibration-damping laminates if measured to work
applications_to_reject_until_later_evide: unverified cosmetic or skin-contact safety claims

success_definition.minimum: A reproducible SCOBY-derived sheet with measured mechanical integrity, acceptable wet-state retention, controlled thickness, documented aging behavior and competitive cost for at least one benign application.
success_definition.strong: A layered SCOBY composite whose strength-to-mass, durability, surface quality and manufacturability are competitive with a low-cost reference material.
success_definition.exceptional: A low-cost SCOBY-derived composite with a clearly demonstrated property combination that is difficult to obtain simultaneously in conventional low-cost sheets, such as useful mechanical performance plus low mass plus moisture durability plus passive EMC utility.

next_gate: REGISTER_A_SMALL_BLINDED_DOE_OF_BASELINE_SCOBY, UNTENSIONED, TENSIONED, AND ONE_LOW-COST_REINFORCED_ARCHITECTURE; MEASURE_IDENTITY, MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES, MOISTURE_RESPONSE, AGING, COST_PER_AREA, AND_BATCH_VARIATION; ONLY THEN SELECT_A_SINGLE_STRUCTURE_FOR_FURTHER_PASSIVE_EMC_CHARACTERIZATION.
authority_rule: This roadmap extends the SCOBY-D0 gating logic without upgrading any hypothesis to established material performance. It intentionally removes weak or sensational application claims and prioritizes inexpensive, reproducible, measurable material science.
